findings.whyThisIsNotCosmetic: The subject's failsIf roster is the operative statement of the conditions under which the artifact is invalid; a later D-000 recording authority reads it to know what the artifact refuses to be read as. A failure roster that names the wrong file in its only OBL-2 / OBL-D1 / OBL-D2 non-closure entry is mis-scoped, not merely mis-worded. The self-trip against failsIf[24] independently forecloses the reading that the label is an accepted shorthand: this revision is the one that made 'This v4 for this subject' a declared failure.
findings.whyThisIsNotDigestDrift: No digest is wrong. All nineteen recordedInputs recompute equal, the subject has not moved, mode is 0444 at start and end, and the pinned OBL sets match leftover-join.v7's live bytes exactly. The defect is confined to the file label inside one failsIf string.
findings.netEffect: The artifact's substantive non-closure position is correct everywhere it is stated in prose — doesNot[8], registerRowNote, authorityClaim, whatThisCloses.leftoverDesignClosedIfAcceptedAndRecorded (empty), leftoverDesignRemainingOnDR101 ([OBL-2, OBL-D1, OBL-D2]), gates2and3Hold (false), and whatThisClosesNote all hold the line. The defect is that the machine-readable failure roster does not, and that the artifact simultaneously declares that defect to be disqualifying.
findings.consequence: A recording cycle that pins this v5 would carry into the record a failsIf roster whose OBL-2 / OBL-D1 / OBL-D2 guard names a frozen, non-recordable predecessor, together with a failsIf[24] rule the recorded bytes visibly breach. Either the roster is enforced and the recording is unlawful on its face, or the roster is not enforced and the subject's other twenty-eight failsIf entries lose their standing as guarantees.
